extracted.intended_audience: states, tribes, public water systems, drinking water professionals, and other stakeholders (public health/community members)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the EPA's Final National Primary Drinking Water Regulation (NPDWR) for six PFAS, including numeric limits (MCLs/MCLGs), monitoring and compliance timelines, notification and treatment obligations, and supporting implementation resources. Intended to guide compliance and implementation by water systems, regulators, and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFOA MCL and MCLG
rubrics_metrics.description: Final MCLG: Zero; Final MCL (enforceable level): 4.0 parts per trillion (ppt) (also expressed as ng/L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PFOA is one of the six PFAS for which EPA established legally enforceable Maximum Contaminant Levels. Compliance with MCLs is determined by running annual averages at the sampling point. EPA also will provide implementation resources and timelines for monitoring and actions if limits are exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFOS MCL and MCLG
rubrics_metrics.description: Final MCLG: Zero; Final MCL (enforceable level): 4.0 ppt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PFOS is regulated with an enforceable MCL and a health-based, non-enforceable MCLG of zero. Compliance determination is by annual averaging at the sampling point; monitoring and implementation timelines apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFHxS MCL and MCLG
rubrics_metrics.description: Final MCLG: 10 ppt; Final MCL (enforceable level): 10 ppt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PFHxS has both a final MCLG and an enforceable MCL set at 10 ppt. The final regulation treats PFHxS as an individually-regulated compound (and also as part of mixtures via a Hazard Index for certain combinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: PFNA MCL and MCLG
rubrics_metrics.description: Final MCLG: 10 ppt; Final MCL (enforceable level): 10 ppt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PFNA is regulated with both MCLG and MCL at 10 ppt. See monitoring, compliance averaging, and implementation timelines for actions required when values exceed these limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: HFPO-DA (GenX) MCL and MCLG
rubrics_metrics.description: Final MCLG: 10 ppt; Final MCL (enforceable level): 10 ppt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFPO-DA (commonly known as GenX) has both MCLG and enforceable MCL set at 10 ppt. It is one of the six PFAS covered by the final NPDWR; monitoring and mitigation requirements apply similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard Index MCL for specified PFAS mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixtures containing two or more of PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA, and PFBS — Final MCLG: 1 (unitless); Hazard Index (enforceable MCL): 1 (unitless).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA established a Hazard Index MCL (unitless) to account for combined and co-occurring levels of these PFAS in drinking water. This applies when two or more of the specified PFAS co-occur and requires assessing combined toxicity via the Hazard Index approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: How compliance is determined
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with MCLs is determined by running annual averages at the sampling point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual averaging at the sampling point is the metric for determining compliance with each enforceable MCL. Water systems must follow the monitoring schedule (initial and ongoing) and use the sampling point annual average to evaluate whether they meet MCLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring requirements and timeline (initial monitoring by 2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems must monitor for these PFAS and have three years to complete initial monitoring (by 2027), followed by ongoing compliance monitoring. Water systems must also provide the public with information on the levels of these PFAS in their drinking water beginning in 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should plan and budget to complete initial monitoring within three years of the rule (by 2027), then continue periodic compliance monitoring per the rule's requirements. Results must be communicated to the public starting in 2027; EPA provides a PFAS NPDWR Monitoring and Reporting fact sheet and other supporting materials to assist systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment/implementation deadline when MCLs exceeded (by 2029)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems have five years (by 2029) to implement solutions that reduce these PFAS if monitoring shows that drinking water levels exceed these MCLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If annual averaged results show exceedances, systems are required to install or implement treatment or other solutions within five years. Planning, procurement, and construction timelines should reflect this deadline; EPA provides treatment options fact sheets and implementation resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation response and public notification (effective in five years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning in five years (2029), public water systems that have PFAS in drinking water which violates one or more of these MCLs must take action to reduce levels of these PFAS in their drinking water and must provide notification to the public of the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems with violations will be required both to remediate (reduce levels) and to notify the public about the violation. Notification and corrective action procedures should follow the Safe Drinking Water Act requirements and the timelines set by the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of federal funding to support implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA announced $1 billion in available funding through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to help states and territories implement PFAS testing and treatment at public water systems and to help owners of private wells address PFAS contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is intended to aid implementation (testing, treatment, private well support). Water systems and states should consult EPA implementation resources and grant guidance to pursue available funds; EPA also references additional implementation resources on its PFAS NPDWR Implementation website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory effect on co-occurring PFAS
rubrics_metrics.description: This regulation will also remove many other PFAS when they co-occur with these regulated PFAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is intended to address not only the six named PFAS but also to remove other PFAS that co-occur with these regulated compounds, particularly via the Hazard Index approach for mixtures.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA announced intents and subsequent regulatory actions (May 14, 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: On May 14, 2025, EPA announced the agency will keep the current National Primary Drinking Water Regulations (NPDWR) for PFOA and PFOS. As part of this action, EPA also announced its intent to extend the PFOA and PFOS Maximum Contaminant Level compliance deadlines and establish a federal exemption framework. Additionally, EPA announced its intent to rescind the regulations and reconsider the regulatory determinations for PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA (commonly known as GenX), and the Hazard Index mixture of these three PFAS plus PFBS to ensure the determinations and any resulting drinking water regulation follow the Safe Drinking Water Act process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are EPA's announced procedural intentions affecting the status, timing, and scope of some parts of the rule. Systems and stakeholders should monitor EPA notices and Federal Register corrections for finalized changes (e.g., any extended deadlines, exemption framework details, or rescissions/reconsiderations).
